{{Top}}
[[File:Xwa-bulk-cruiser.jpg|thumb|250px|A bulk [[Cruiser/Legends|cruiser]]]]
{{Quote|I've outrun Imperial starships. Not the local bulk cruisers mind you, I'm talking about the big Corellian ships now.|[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]|<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
A '''bulk cruiser''' was a [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]] design that combined attributes of both [[Warship/Legends|warships]] and [[Cargo hauler/Legends|cargo haulers]]. They saw service in both the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] of the [[Great Galactic War]], as well as the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance]] navies of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].

==Characteristics==
[[File:DamagedBulkCruiser-EitEDabgCiv.png|left|thumb|250pox|A heavily damaged bulk cruiser in orbit of a planet]]
Several different models existed, like the [[Neutron Star-class bulk cruiser/Legends|''Neutron Star''-]] and [[Battle Horn-class bulk cruiser|''Battle Horn''-classes]], but the overall design was relatively the same, with an armament of thirty [[Quad laser cannon/Legends|quad laser cannons]]&mdash;ten forward, ten to port, and ten to starboard&mdash;and two forward [[Tractor beam/Legends|tractor beam]] projectors. The bulk cruiser's large and bulbous forward section contained a medium sized hangar for up to one squadron of starfighters.

==History==
[[Keizar-Volvec bulk cruiser|One kind]] of bulk cruiser was produced by [[Keizar-Volvec/Legends|Keizar-Volvec]] and used by the Sith Empire as a [[Command ship/Legends|command ship]] during the Great Galactic War.<ref name="TOR:FA">''[[The Old Republic: Fatal Alliance]]''</ref> Bulk cruisers were used by the [[Old Republic shipping fleet]]; when [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]] made the [[P2-series astromech droid]] available exclusively to the [[Merchant/Legends|merchant]] [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]] on a trial basis, the P2 units proved to be capable maintenance units aboard the vessels.<ref name="EGTD">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

The more famous designs were produced during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], meant to be second-line [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] ships.<ref name="TFUCG">''[[The Force Unleashed Campaign Guide]]''</ref> Not deployed until after the conflict was over, they became among some of the most common designs seen in space, although most were modified, due to their stock design being prone to breakdowns, slow speed and expensive refueling.<ref name="TFUCG" /> The term came to be used to describe a number of ships that fit the general characteristics.<ref name="RASB">[[The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''The Rebel Alliance Sourcebook'', Second Edition]]</ref>

Modifications to the ships to make them more battleworthy were often seen as useless by Alliance [[Commander/Legends|commanders]]. Instead, most were converted into carrier cruisers, with extensive docking bays and repair facilities. The crews were told to stay out of any serious engagements and rely upon their [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] squadrons as their primary weapons. Bulk cruisers that were converted into carriers were capable of carrying three squadrons of fighters. Other ships were kept as escorts for Alliance convoys.<ref name="RASB" />

The Empire<ref name="ANH" /> and various corporations kept bulk cruisers as patrol vessels, guarding systems where important corporate assets were to be found. In addition, these ships were used to track down Rebel ships and combat pirate-attacks on convoys.<ref name="TFUCG" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] mentioned outrunning bulk cruisers in [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']]. [[West End Games]] took that remark and built an RPG profile on these ships.
